Priority tasks

1

Add the module linking to all centers from the home page

This widget should appear on the home page, but removing the province before the city name and/or “prettifying” the names a bit. In Granada, for example, perhaps just “Granada”.

2

Two types of page for cities: /pages/ and /collections/

54 center collections, one per center. In addition, 7 cities have their own page (/pages/).

In Shopify, each center has its own collection (the /pages/centros listing links to 54), and some cities also have a city page. Both target similar searches, something like “laser hair removal in [city]”, but they are different URLs.

Why it matters

  • In the August 30 SERP tracking, grupostop.com appears 27 times in the top 10: 21 with center collections and none with a page.
  • Barcelona and Madrid, the two largest cities, use a page, and across their 14 and 13 keywords no grupostop.com URL appears in the top 10.
  • Cities with more than one center have a city page as well as collections for their centers. In Barcelona, the city page and the “Bcn Eixample” collection target the same search, so there is cannibalization and Google does not know which URL to rank.
  • The competitor Láserum has a single URL per city and totals 289 appearances in the top 10.

The appearance and content data come from the keyword pull selected in August and its analysis, with a single date and a single fetch per page type. On their own they do not prove that the template is the cause.

Decision to agree

Resolve the duplication between the city page and the collections of its centers.

There is no single action: it has business and marketing implications and must be agreed. The possible approaches are:

  • Create a single page per city and redirect the others to it.
  • Keep both and add canonicals pointing to the URL that should rank.
  • Keep both with a different intent: the city for the general search and each center for its area, linked to each other.
  • Other possible solutions...

5

Reduce the HTML weight below Googlebot's limit

PageUncompressed HTMLCompressed (Brotli)Inline JS% of the 2 MB limit
/products/depilacion-laser-hombre3.52 MB0.21 MB3.05 MB176%
/products/tratamiento-regenerador-facial3.50 MB0.20 MB2.98 MB175%
/collections/depilacion-laser-estetica-vigo3.17 MB0.15 MB2.83 MB159%
/collections/depilacion-laser-estetica-bilbao3.11 MB0.15 MB2.76 MB155%
/collections/depilacion-laser-estetica-tarragona3.11 MB0.15 MB2.76 MB155%
/pages/centros-depilacion-laser-estetica-barcelona3.03 MB0.13 MB2.74 MB151%
/pages/centros-depilacion-laser-sevilla3.02 MB0.13 MB2.74 MB151%

Measured on October 20 from the browser, not as Googlebot, and not counting HTTP headers.

What Google says about the limit

  • Googlebot for Search crawls the first 2 MB of an HTML file. For PDFs the limit is 64 MB.
  • The limit applies to uncompressed data. The HTML dropping to 0.13–0.21 MB with Brotli doesn't help: Google counts the already decompressed HTML.
  • When it reaches the cap, Googlebot stops crawling and sends only what it has already downloaded for indexing. Whatever comes after the cut may be ignored: content, links, FAQ or schema.
  • External CSS and JS are crawled separately, each with its own limit, and do not count toward the HTML's 2 MB.
  • The 15 MB sometimes cited is the default limit for Google's other crawlers, not the one for Googlebot for Search. Google clarified this in its documentation in February 2026.
  • Google does not recommend any margin below 2 MB. As a target I propose staying under 1.5 MB, so as not to touch the limit. That is my own criterion, not a Google figure.

Main offenders in the HTML

  • Inline JavaScript is between 85% and 91% of the HTML, from 2.74 to 3.05 MB per page. It is almost identical across all of them, so it is a block common to the whole site.
  • The men's landing page has 68 inline scripts. Two of them add up to 2.66 MB (1.43 MB and 1.23 MB), 75% of the HTML. Judging by the keywords they contain, one looks like a theme or app bundle and the other store and center data. Their content has not been reviewed.
  • The rest weighs little: inline CSS between 0.09 and 0.15 MB, SVG between 0.04 and 0.10 MB and JSON-LD under 0.01 MB.

What to do

Action

Take the inline JavaScript out of the HTML and optimize it.

It is what removes between 85% and 91% of the weight. First audit what each large script is (on the men's landing page, two add up to 2.66 MB), remove what isn't used, minify it and move it to external files with caching and loading with defer or async. Large data, such as the center listing, goes into a JSON that is loaded only when needed. Then measure again.

Each external file has its own 2 MB limit, and the two large scripts fit. Pending: measure at which byte each key element falls (h1, content, JSON-LD, FAQ, footer).

6

CDN Improvements

< 100 ms The TTFB needs to come down to under 100 ms.

Why it matters

  • Search Console measures an average response time of 565 ms on Googlebot's HTML requests, far from the 100 ms we are aiming for.
  • Google adjusts how much it crawls a site according to how fast the server responds. With slow responses it crawls fewer pages in the same time.
  • The TTFB (time to first byte) is the first stretch of every page load, and users feel it too.

How to do it

  1. Read the Cloudflare logs and analyze the hit ratio, that is, what share of requests is served from cache and which reach the origin server.
  2. Identify what is causing that high number: which types of URL are not cached, or bypass the cache, and how much they weigh in Googlebot's requests.
  3. Improve Cloudflare's caching rules so those URLs are served from cache. That should be enough.
7

Crawl budget

Google is crawling thousands of URLs that return 404.

These URLs should return a 410 error: they are the ones of the form grupostop.com/[numeric-ID].

https://grupostop.com/52189144349

A 404 is fine, but the right one is 410: it is the way to tell Google that this URL will not come back and that it should remove it from its index.

Goal

That Google crawls the URLs that matter to the business and not those that have no value.

Google is requesting WordPress URLs

  • Add the WordPress URLs to robots.txt with disallow.
  • Return a 403 to bots on those URLs, so the 404 error is never served. The 403 must be returned by Cloudflare.

Cloudflare WAF custom rule with the Block action (returns 403). Cloudflare documentation.

9

Optimize the content of product landing pages and center pages

Decide what content to add based on Hotjar data: what the user needs to see in order to convert into a booking or purchase.

Starting pages
Landing page · grupostop.com/products/depilacion-laser-hombre Center · grupostop.com/collections/depilacion-laser-estetica-albacete

How to do it with Hotjar data

  1. Segment by mobile and desktop, traffic source and new or returning user, and define what counts as a conversion: booking an appointment or purchase.
  2. Scroll maps: see how far down the user gets and whether they reach reviews, FAQs, prices and the closing “I already have sessions” or “I want to book”.
  3. Click maps: see which blocks get clicked and where there are dead or repeated clicks, for example on promotions, most requested areas or the center selector.
  4. Recordings of sessions that don't convert: look for doubts, going back and forth between blocks and the exact point where they leave.
First hypothesis

A widget explaining how many sessions are needed depending on the body area.

The men's landing page says the number depends on each person and that men usually need more sessions, but it gives no figures per area. The most requested areas shown on the page itself are:

  • Back
  • Chest
  • Abdomen
  • Shoulders
  • Intimate area
  • Legs

The session figures have to come from the medical team. Hotjar will tell us whether this question really comes up before booking.

10

Important schemas still need to be added to the center pages

Action

Add the MedicalClinic and Physician schemas to the center pages.

The goal is to mark those URLs as what they are, a clinic, and to state who the medical lead of each one is. This matters in terms of E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness and Trustworthiness).

Current situation

  • The site already has schema. All the pages reviewed load the brand's MedicalOrganization block, with WebSite and BreadcrumbList. The product landing page adds a Service.
  • The center collections add CollectionPage, FAQPage and LocalBusiness, and the LocalBusiness only carries name and url. The city pages only carry WebPage, without LocalBusiness or FAQPage.
  • What is missing is medical staff markup (neither Physician nor Person) on any of them.

Which types to use

Center or clinic MedicalClinic

It inherits from MedicalBusiness and MedicalOrganization. It supports medicalSpecialty, availableService and employee, which is used to link to the center's staff.

Professional IndividualPhysician + Person

IndividualPhysician provides practicesAt, which points to the center where the professional practices. Combined with Person, jobTitle, hasCredential, worksFor, alumniOf and memberOf are added.

Rules for marking it up properly

  • Mark up only what the page shows: name, job title, qualification and specialty.
  • The medicalSpecialty values must come from schema.org's MedicalSpecialty list.
  • Give each professional their own identifier and link it in both directions: the center points to the professional (employee) and the professional to the center (practicesAt).
What to expect from Google

Google documents LocalBusiness markup: name and address are required, and it recommends geo, telephone, url and openingHoursSpecification. That documentation shows no rich result specific to doctors, so the value of this markup lies in making the entities (center and professionals) clear, not in a rich result.

What is needed to implement it

  • At least one professional per center, with job title, qualification and specialty, and their consent to be published.
  • Complete the center's LocalBusiness, which currently only has name and url: address, coordinates, opening hours and phone.
  • Validate with the Rich Results Test and Search Console's URL inspection, and with the validator.schema.org tool.

Minor tasks

Long tail keyword study

Run a study of the long tail keywords and decide what actions to take to rank for each of them.

It is also important to address the “People also search for” searches and work out how to fit them in and how to approach them.

Optimize blog pages for Google Discover

The blog pages can end up appearing in Google Discover, especially if they are worked with that goal, and that can bring some traffic when offers and promotions are launched. In addition, Search Console shows that GrupoSTOP has already appeared in Discover at some point, an advantage worth taking up.

grupostop.com/blogs/novedades/pastillas-anticonceptivas-y-depilacion-laser Instructions for appearing in Google Discover

Appear in Groupon.es URLs

Groupon.es has high visibility on the most transactional keywords. Appearing in those URLs could also be interesting.

Add speculationrules to prefetch the next page

The center collections do not prefetch the next page: there are no prefetch or prerender rules. Adding a speculationrules block lets the browser load in the background the page the user is going to visit, making navigation almost instant. It would be limited to center collections and landing pages.

Prerender pages in Chrome for instant page navigations

Linking to treatments from the centers page

This module should link to the treatment and, if possible, pre-select in the form the center the user comes from, to remove one step from the user's conversion.

Reminder

URLs with 2 redirects

After a migration it is normal to lose traffic and recover it later.

In this case there is one URL, and there are more, that has changed address several times during the process. The redirects are in place, but changing a URL is not the most suitable thing for SEO.

With a double URL change, this chart can be normal. At some point you have to be patient until Google finishes understanding the new URL structure and forgets the old one.
